title: Etekcity 0.1g Food Kitchen Scale, Bowl, Digital Grams and Ounces for Weight Loss, Dieting, Baking, Cooking, and Meal Prep, 11lb/5kg, Stainless Steel Silver
description:
About this item

reviews_5s:
I ordered this scale to replace my prior etekcity scale that lasted about 3 years until the buttons began wearing out causing intermittent issues. (It still measures accurately, just won't consistently turn on or tare anymore even with new batteries).

I chose this specific model because it's one of the few available that promised accuracy down to 1 gram because it's ridiculous to have a scale that doesn't register small amounts. (A different etekcity scale was returned for that specific issue).

This model has Accurate and Consistent readings even at 1 gram. Bowl works great as a cover.

Silver weighing surface helps prevent the black scale from disappearing on my black cutting board, Win-Win!This is the best kitchen scale I have ever owned. It's the perfect size. I've used it a number of times and it's perfect every single time. It's sensitive and so easy to use. It is definitely well made and high quality. It's really attractive so I can just leave it on my kitchen countertop. Also, shipping was very fast. I definitely recommend this scale.This is a great scale.Easy to use and seems to be very accurate. It is obviously well-made! When I received it and opened the box , I was extremely impressed with the effort that went in to packaging the product to prevent damage while shopping it. I highly recommend this item.Very nice for the price . I really like the scale because it has that stainless steel bowl that sits right on top making it so much easier to measure food.10/10. reviews_1s:
I ordered this after seeing it had great reviews. But as I started using it for baking and other small quantity measurements I needed, it is not accurate and it changes the weight of the same thing, every time you place it on the scale. If I weigh 10 grams of something, take it off the scale and put it back on- it weighs differently EVERY TIME. Unfortunately I had missed my 30 day return slot, and I have to buy something new that actually works and throw this one away because it’s really just useless.
Not sure how it got so many good reviews, maybe just mine has a defect, but I surely do not recommend this at all.The stainless steel version with the stainless steel bowl does not measure tenths of a gram. It only measures whole grams. I bought it to measure tea and it's not precise enough. It will jump from 0 to 2g or 0 to 4g when I'm measuring the loose tea. I wanted something more precise.

If you don't need to measure very small amounts, it's great.It takes quite a long time for the measurement to stop changing, around 30 seconds. Then, it continues to adjust, sometimes substantially. I don't feel like I can trust any measurement from this scale. After pressing Tare, the scale goes to 0, and then might continue down into the negatives. If I knew before I bought it, for a scale of this quality, I would not pay more than $5.00. I will never purchase another product from this company. I will be throwing away this scale and buying another from a more reputable company.When you see the same exact unit under multiple names from different companies you know that they were bulk purchased from China. I turned it on and the numbers were bouncing around like a one-arm bandit slot machine. For the times I can get it to stabilize at a number, this second I put anything on its away the numbers start bouncing around again. It's junk. I wouldn't even give you a dollar for it because it's 100% useless. For the lucky ones who got a unit that works, you could have got a better unit with the same money.Wanna do a fun experiment?
1- Turn on your brand new scale. Digits should show 0.
2- Pick up the janky plastic bowl that feels like it will break in your hand if you sneeze around it; Scale = - 50 grams or something.
3- Put the bowl back on the scale; Scale = 22 grams. Wow! Your bowl just got much heavier while you held it!
Or maybe there is more air in it now? Mindblowing.
4- Reset the scale to zero.
5- Say, place a clementine on it; Scale= 50 g
6- Remove the clementine; Scale= -30 g.
7- Repeat steps 5 and 6 a few times until you get to -150 grams just for kicks.
8- Throw the scale back into it's box and get a refund.
9- Enjoy!
Other fun facts:
- The weight number often doesn't stabilizes and goes up and down randomly long after you changed any weight on it. I'm not talking of air changes causing fractions of weight change but up to 10 grams up or down difference.
- Since it's so precise it detects the invisible, it is probably a good astral detector. If you're in a pinch and need to locate a ghost's position but are out of your usual DOTS projector or motion detector, this could come in handy. Monitor the scale and if you get a sudden 120 grams increase or so, boom, you probably got a ghost on your scale.I bought the scale because it can measure 0.1g, and it worked well in the 1st month. What made me mad is the seller lied to me and said “If the total weight of the food you're testing doesn't reach 1g, the scale won't be able to measure it”. The fact is sometimes it can read when it’s 0.8g but sometimes it shows zero when it’s actually more than 1g. Anyway, don’t buy it. Young kittens tend to cozy down so you can grab a weight and if you put older kittens in it front first, you can grab a weight before they sort things out though to get away.was excited to get this. that ended literally the first 30 minutes into using it.

i'll note the most biggest problem with it right away. first time ever using it. don't even use it for 30 minutes and i am already cleaning it up, packing it up, hitting return product, and getting my money back on a gift card. the unit button, which is supposed to change it from ounces, to grams, to whatever. doesn't work AT ALL. i tried holding it, double-pressing it quick, i tried putting some stuff in there while it was on ounces, so it had something in there, then tried pressing the unit button thinking maybe it would register and just convert it to grams. nope. unit button just doesn't work at all whatsoever right out of the frickin box.

i was cutting some chicken into little chunks and it was falling right into the bowl. cutting chicken right over the bowl, pieces are falling into the bowl every 2 to 4 seconds. the weight keeps going up, i keep cutting no breaks no long pauses, great. suddenly it just shuts off. as if the weight wasn't constantly going up, as if it hadn't been in use. that is not what i look for in a scale. it should have realized i was using it and not shut off on me.

even if the unit button had worked, the fact that it shut off on me right in the middle of adding food to it is enough to make me want to get something else.
